data.name: Jada
data.gender_notes: Jada is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word ‘yadah’, meaning ‘to know’ or ‘to give thanks’. In the Bible, Jada is the name of a woman who was the wife of King Boaz and the mother of Obed, who was the grandfather of King David. The name Jada carries the meaning “Gentle, Just” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Jada usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle, just and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing wisdom, understanding, and gratitude.
data.etymology: Jada belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle, Just.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jada total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_latin.name: Jada

in_english.name: Jada
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jada originates from the Hebrew root 'yada', meaning 'he knows' or 'helper'. It carries connotations of wisdom, insight, and assistance. While not directly mentioned in the Bible, its etymological roots are deeply biblical. Historically, the name has been used across various Christian cultures, symbolizing spiritual awareness and support. The name Jada is often associated with qualities of compassion, understanding, and guidance.
